cards.text: A psalm writer is calling people to sing to the LORD a new song. And he is NOT inviting one little choir in one little town.

cards.question: The singer calls for a new song to the LORD. Who does he call to sing it?

cards.text: ALL THE EARTH, friend, and I could never get six cookie cutters to sing on key at one birthday batch. Next he says sing to the LORD, bless His name and proclaim His salvation.

cards.question: The singer says to proclaim the LORD's salvation. How often?

cards.text: And this news isn't meant to stay home. He wants the LORD's glory and wonders carried WAY past his own front door.

cards.question: The singer wants the LORD's glory and wonders declared among the ___.

cards.text: Why all this singing? Here's the reason, friend: the LORD is great, and greatly to be praised.

cards.question: The singer says the LORD is to be feared above all gods.
Then the singer says what all the gods of the nations really are. What does he call them?

cards.text: Idols, friend, and it's the LORD who made the heavens. Calling an idol a god is like that dead battery I shared the junk drawer with, swearing it still had enough charge to run the WHOLE KITCHEN.

cards.question: Next the singer pictures the LORD's sanctuary. He says strength and beauty fill it.

cards.text: Now the singer calls out to someone directly. He tells them to ascribe glory and strength to the LORD.

cards.question: Who does the singer call to ascribe glory and strength to the LORD?
The singer tells the families of the nations to stay outside the LORD's courts.

cards.text: Come on IN, and bring an offering! The nations are being called in, and friend, the only time I ever got called in, it came to the back of a junk drawer in the middle of the night.
Then: "Worship the LORD in the splendor of His holiness; tremble before Him, all the earth." After that, the singer gives the nations a short announcement to spread.

cards.question: What announcement does the singer want declared among the nations?
Right after the news that the LORD reigns, the singer says the world is firmly established and cannot be ___.
The singer says the LORD will judge the peoples. How will He judge them?

cards.text: Then the singer looks past the people, up to the sky and out to the sea.

cards.question: The singer calls on the heavens and the earth to keep silent before the LORD.

cards.text: The sea resounds, the fields exult, and then the trees of the forest sing for joy. TREES, friend, with no mouths, no lungs and no sheet music, singing before I've pulled my first batch out of the oven!

cards.question: Why does the singer say the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD?

answers.text: He is coming to judge the earth
The harvest has finally come in
The long winter is finally over

cards.text: And the singer says it twice: He is coming, He is coming. Friend, when a man says it twice, I'm not checking the calendar, I'm checking that my ovens are HOT.

cards.question: When He comes, the singer says the LORD will judge the world in ___ and the peoples in His ___.

findings.problem: The setup line "he is NOT inviting one little choir in one little town" rules out two of card 2's wrong answers before the baker picks. "The people of Jerusalem" is one town, and "The priests in the temple" is one choir. Only "All the earth" is left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new backstory moment. It says Papa Dorin tried to get his six cookie cutters to sing on key at a birthday batch in the Millers' kitchen. The backstory only says Sparkle hummed to the oven. Jokes may make up small moments around his bakery, not new events in his past with the kids.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The setup "carried WAY past his own front door" rules out card 6's wrong answers, "priests" and "elders", because both are groups close to home. It points straight at "nations", so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. In his backstory Papa Dorin was called OUT of the drawer ("I've been called out of the drawer"). Here he says he got "called in" and that the call "came to the back of a junk drawer", which is confusing. A stranger would say "huh?" It also blurs his own invitation with the nations entering the courts.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out by tone. "With equity" is the only good quality, and "With harshness" and "In haste" are faults a baker would reject for the LORD without reasoning from the passage.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card turns the psalm's calls and future into present fact. The text says "let the sea resound", "Let the fields exult" and "Then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy". The card says "The sea resounds, the fields exult". The joke then has the trees "singing before I've pulled my first batch out of the oven", as if they are singing now. Verse 13 ties their singing to the LORD's coming.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The two blanks test wording, not meaning. "Righteousness" and "faithfulness" fit either blank equally well, so which word goes where can only be guessed from the exact line. A baker who swaps them could argue they're right.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The right answers stand out by tone. "Righteousness" and "faithfulness" are the only good qualities. The wrong words "fury", "secrecy" and "silence" are all negative or odd, so the baker can pick the right ones without reasoning from the passage.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
